Mail login requires an encrypted verified connection; changing its host or port requires the password again, changing a provider issuer requires its client secret again, and an issuer already used for sign-in cannot change. A mail server or provider endpoint change cannot reuse the saved secret silently. A login for SMTP cannot be saved over an unencrypted connection.

Mail retries start after 30 seconds and double to one hour, permanently refused recipients fail at once and other failures stop after 24 hours; queued message text is sealed and erased when finished, and an administrator can stop a waiting message.

Bulk grants are separate writes, so refused grants leave successful grants in place and retain the failed choice with its reason; bulk group removal is atomic and refuses removal of the last active human Security administrator, including one granted through a group.

Consumer parent fields use the object’s output names; a parent whose type is unexposed has a null public type, and projection objectType fields require every reachable type to be exposed.

A model operation request applies up to 500 operations atomically as one recorded step at the draft version, stores inverses and diagnostics and allows intermediate invalid drafts. Impact counts cover live data and open change sets only in workspaces running that draft’s model (R115)

Installing a model draft makes the installed release its base without resetting its version; reinstalling the same model key and version is a conflict, so the install dialog proposes an editable next version.

The layout preview reads chosen live data through the draft’s model, uses an empty record for a new type and disables writes; invalid drafts cannot preview, and layout edits are ordinary undoable draft steps. A model preview never writes and cannot open an invalid draft.
Turning off XREF in the consumer editor asks for confirmation, removes its match rules and turns off Resolve; draft schema, example and OpenAPI documents are available before installation.

Uploading a source file replaces its owner’s current file, retains the superseded file for job retention, profiles every filled cell and deletes files with their owner; deleting a file first stops every job reading it.
A load-affecting model or profile step replaces the current dry run; labels, navigation, release identity, layout and consumer definitions do not cancel a running dry run or start another.

Model operations update the draft’s import profile too: renamed references follow, moved or split fields acquire matching sources, merges repoint sources, and removals leave unmapped columns with warnings rather than silently ignoring them.

Missing named parent or related records can be created once per value during loading, but missing:create requires matching by name; fixed source parents cannot also be bound by a parent column. A source cannot bind its parent both as a fixed value and as a column. Automatic creation of a missing named parent or related record requires a name match.

A rules-based proposal explains its pattern, evidence, alternatives and requirements; repeated inference updates only unedited proposals, preserves administrator edits and undone decisions, and reports disagreements instead of replaying them.

Workbook checks report new, missing or renamed columns, new lookup values, name drift and missing records before loading; a rename candidate keeps its column position and shares at least half the values.

Deleting records missing from a workbook requires a change set, excludes records named by refused rows, and refuses surviving descendants or required dependants; single-valued relationship mappings replace their old targets on the next load.
A source may skip rows without keys only when it declares a key; its binding report and dry run count skipped rows, while empty source rows and identified heading or note rows do not create records.

Laid-out workbook lists can be adjusted by header, last row and columns, unloaded or read from a chosen rectangle; column bindings follow their original letters, and three matching lists under one title can be read as a parent list with contained records.

A migration preview holds the live rows it converts while it runs, so writes to those rows wait; confirmation binds the workspace assignment and feed position, requires explicit acceptance of loss and switches data and release atomically. A migration preview can make writes to its live records wait.

Moving a change set to the workspace’s release rebases its converted content onto current live data without changing live data or its feed; conflicting authored records, relationships and mapping sets are refused before its base and pin change together. A change-set migration targets only its workspace’s current release.

Migrating a workspace to a change set’s release and publishing it is one transaction whose confirmation also binds that change set’s version and the active publication; neither half can succeed alone.

Import profiles belong to one model and are invalid in workspaces running another; installing a draft cannot overwrite another model’s profile key, and new-model drafts have no unrelated data impact. A profile belongs to one model and cannot load into another model’s workspace.
A model draft compares with its base, otherwise the latest installed release of its own model, otherwise an empty model; draft-operation impact is limited to workspaces running that model.

A retired model release cannot be selected for new use, but existing workspaces and change sets keep working and may retain their own release; the default workspace’s release cannot retire, exact reinstallation restores a release, and deletion requires no running, history, profile or mapping reference. A retired release remains valid for existing users but cannot be chosen for new use elsewhere.

Before 1.0 each engine release reads only its current schema language, now 0.10; an older stored release can be previewed and raised in place against its hash through the workspace screen or model_release_raise, while invalid or duplicate results are refused.

A profile’s uploaded file and latest check are isolated by workspace, require Bulk there, and cannot supersede another workspace’s file; check routes require workspaceKey and read no file or check when that workspace has none.

Edit model from a workspace reuses its current remembered draft, otherwise an eligible draft or a new one, with at most one remembered draft per workspace; a model change elsewhere detaches the old draft without deleting it.

Apply to a workspace lists model changes, data impact, change sets left behind and other workspaces left unchanged; it installs and activates there or opens a migration preview, and a failed activation retries against the installed release without reinstalling.

A composite import key uses two or more column-bound attributes together; duplicate stored combinations are ambiguous, blank components are missing keys and unbound components are refused, while batch upsert keys remain unchanged. A composite import key must have every component bound and filled and must identify at most one stored record.

The model editor can list a type in another application and create, change or remove a relation matrix with only structurally possible choices, adding the needed type listings in the same step while records stay in their owning applications.

An unused released element may be removed or changed when its impact is zero, but a released key stays fixed; removals clean up dependent views and panels and the issues list identifies every remaining broken page.

Repeated workbook headings remain separately addressable by column names with numbered suffixes; compatible repeated keys merge across sources, existing-record sources can find values written by another source, and a related-record parent column can use a value map.

A changed profile key colliding with another model is shown as an issue before installation, with an offered free key and editable key and name; replacing a profile of the same model saves its next version.

A change of a change set’s model release protects unsaved input, reloads the pinned model before enabling writes, clears obsolete cursors and opens a model-declared destination if the old page no longer exists; refresh failures explain whether the pin already changed.

Creating a mapping target asks for its application, offers parents only in that application and refuses creation when no required parent type can stand there; creation selects the new target but the mapping changes only after Save.
A selected mapping target retains values when attributes are omitted; an explicit object replaces all values and an empty object clears them only if valid.

A matrix cell reports its complete count and previews at most five records; condition-based inactive and uniqueness-conflict states apply only in the outgoing direction. A matrix previews at most five cell records while reporting the full count. Incoming matrix reads have neither inactive nor uniqueness-conflict states from rules on the binding’s target end.

Restructuring offers values and relationships back only from effective reclassifications in the current or published change sets, keeps restored relationship IDs, and does not restore deliberately cleared values or discarded work. Lost values are restored from effective reclassifications, not from deliberate clears or discarded change sets.
A tree drop chooses a parent or hierarchy level rather than a manual ordering slot; moving several selected records together requires their types to stay the same.

Lists sort by name when no sort is selected; any non-JSON attribute may sort regardless of its sortable flag, with missing fields last across types; computed paths and unrecorded timestamps cannot sort.
A changed record opened under its old type is refused with its current type in the selected context, and the browser follows the current route; review filters match either its before or after type.
Matrix link and move candidates remain listed when ineligible, with a reason; when a stale edit finds the record gone from its cell, the dialog returns to that cell’s actions with an explanation.

A change-set review has separate Records and Relationships lists with before/after values and paths, URL-held tab, filters and position; each page reads one snapshot and removed records use their source type.

Attribute mapping during restructuring accepts equal value types or lossless text-to-long-text and integer-to-decimal widening; values that fail the destination rules become inputs, and values without a place remain in history.

Blank ordinary attribute and owned-record workbook cells leave values unchanged; an empty replace-relationship cell clears its set, and several owned records under one parent form a read-only summary cell. A cleared workbook cell changes nothing unless it replaces a relationship set.
A columns-per-parent workbook exceeding Excel’s 16,384-column limit fails INVALID_EXPORT_LAYOUT when its export job runs.

A sampled bulk deletion confirms only the items whose impacts were previewed; other deletes need their own preview and are refused at execution. A sampled deletion preview cannot authorise items it did not preview.

Job preview confirmation is refused immediately after retention expires, even before the sweep marks it expired; execution rechecks the stored file, versions and context and remains authoritative over a sample preview. An expired preview cannot be confirmed even if its status still says awaiting confirmation.

An editable multi-valued relationship cell saves additions and removals in one atomic batch; single-valued cells use candidate choices, and computed, ancestor, containment, ownership, read-only and publication cells offer no edit controls.

Model mappings save type, field, relationship, parent, default, match and value-map decisions as versioned undoable steps, report omissions and invalid references, and propose matches using shared unique values of every declared type.

Copy and move previews cover every selected item and list conversions, lost fields, read-only fields, missing effective periods, duplicates and refusals; a changed mapping or workspace release requires a fresh dry run.

A confirmed copy loads a new target change set; Move also prepares source deletions, retaining records edited since preview or still required by records that stay, and the copy must publish before those deletions.
Copies retain record origins so later copies update earlier copies and a move back updates the original or recreates its original ID; reports and history name each source record.

Only visible rows and nearby rows are drawn in long lists, while their own search covers the full collection; browser Find sees only drawn rows, and table edit controls are available on the focused row or every row on touch. Browser Find searches only drawn rows of a long list.

Holding a tree record still for half a second starts a touch drag; movement first scrolls and a short tap opens, edge zones scroll while dragging, a stationary release opens the sidebar node menu, and read-only or publication trees cannot drag.

Expanding a hierarchy node automatically opens one additional child level only when it has a sole expandable child; keyboard movement preserves focus and the rail remembers its position within each workspace and application.

A technical workbook is separate from a workbook for people; the latter exports all related records, marks columns it cannot load back, uses a hidden import profile and version columns, and replaces overlong or ambiguous cells with read-only summaries pointing to their sheets.

An open change set is shared by authorised workers regardless of creator; submitting freezes it, including release moves, unless the same transaction withdraws its request, and only the submitter or an approver may withdraw.

Approval publishes atomically against the submitted version and current publication; send-back requires a comment, secondPerson forbids deciding one’s own request, and migration-and-publish follows the same Publish and approval checks.

Notice email is off until enabled and needs configured mail and the person’s address; immediate mail includes only unread notices made since enabling and less than 24 hours old, with links but no record or person content, and disabling email leaves inbox notices intact.

The bell shows at most twenty unread notices; Notifications retains searchable history with kind, workspace, read-state and sort choices, supports bulk read/unread/delete, and permanently deleting notices leaves their subjects intact.

Opening a job, move, migration or change-set review marks that person’s subject notices read, including notices arriving while it is open; deciding a request or confirming or cancelling a waiting job closes the waiting notice, and notices expire after 90 days.

A record’s history groups changes by day with expandable before/after values, kind and actor filters, ten initial entries and twenty more at a time; publication or type-change entries explicitly say when earlier values were not recorded.

A digest has no 24-hour notice cutoff: it includes eligible unread, unhandled notices since email was enabled, counts them all and lists the newest fifty; job lines add retained applied and rejected counts without names. A digest has no twenty-four-hour cutoff for eligible unread notices.
A digest’s next time is absent when no schedule exists or email is off; enabling email recalculates it, a changed frequency or time zone moves it and repeating the same settings preserves it.

Following defaults off, is idempotent and requires Browse; losing Browse or deactivation stops notices but keeps the follow choice, so publication notices resume if access returns, and clients never follow.

A publication notice opens its publication only while it is active and the person can browse; otherwise opening it marks it read and leaves the inbox in place, including when followed from a digest link.

Import and Export are in the workspace menu beside Edit model; export keeps the collection’s type, filters, parent and columns, while opening from another page offers application types and collection text search remains excluded.

Relationship filters can include or exclude records having a related record below an ancestor at any depth in live, change-set and publication data; live created and updated timestamps can filter without view declarations, and ranges show each condition.
